claim: The lysosome plays an important role in maintaining cellular nutrient homeostasis.
source: The lysosome plays an important role in maintaining cellular nutrient homeostasis.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about lysosome function.

claim: Regulation of nutrient storage can occur by the ubiquitination of certain transporters that are then sorted into the lysosome lumen for degradation.
source: Regulation of nutrient storage can occur by the ubiquitination of certain transporters that are then sorted into the lysosome lumen for degradation.
evidence: This statement is supported by the research findings presented in the manuscript and references to prior work.

claim: Genetic screens uncovered genes that encode a ubiquitin ligase complex, components of the PtdIns 3-kinase complex, and the ESCRT machinery.
source: These screens uncovered genes that encode a ubiquitin ligase complex, components of the PtdIns 3-kinase complex, and the ESCRT machinery.
evidence: This is directly stated as a result of the genetic screens performed in the study.

claim: Ubiquitinated vacuole membrane proteins recruit ESCRTs to the vacuole surface.
source: These tests revealed that ubiquitinated vacuole membrane proteins recruit ESCRTs to the vacuole surface, where they mediate cargo sorting and direct cargo delivery into the vacuole lumen.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the RapiDeg system tests.

claim: ESCRTs mediate cargo sorting and direct cargo delivery into the vacuole lumen at the vacuole surface.
source: These tests revealed that ubiquitinated vacuole membrane proteins recruit ESCRTs to the vacuole surface, where they mediate cargo sorting and direct cargo delivery into the vacuole lumen.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the RapiDeg system tests.

claim: ESCRTs can function at both the late endosome and the vacuole membrane to mediate cargo sorting and intra-luminal vesicle formation.
source: Our findings demonstrate that the ESCRTs can function at both the late endosome and the vacuole membrane to mediate cargo sorting and intra-luminal vesicle formation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: The lysosomal membrane contains various transporters that mediate the efflux and influx of ions and nutrients across the lysosomal membrane.
source: Similar to the plasma membrane (PM), the lysosomal membrane contains various transporters that mediate the efflux and influx of ions and nutrients across the lysosomal membrane (Xu and Ren, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Dysregulation of lysosomal transporters underlies the pathogenesis of many inherited metabolic disorders in humans termed lysosomal storage diseases.
source: Dysregulation of lysosomal transporters underlies the pathogenesis of many inherited metabolic disorders in humans termed lysosomal storage diseases (LSDs), such as Niemann-Pick disease, Salla disease, Cystinosis, and mucolipidosis (Gahl et al., 2002; Parkinson-Lawrence et al., 2010; Schulze and Sandhoff, 2011; Vitner et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The precise regulation of lysosomal membrane proteins is crucial to maintain nutrient and ion balance in the cell.
source: The precise regulation of lysosomal membrane proteins is therefore crucial to maintain nutrient and ion balance in the cell.
evidence: This is an inference based on the established role of lysosomal transporters and the consequences of their dysregulation.

claim: The vacuole membrane lysine transporter Ypq1 is ubiquitinated after lysine withdrawal by Rsp5, a Nedd4 family HECT-type E3 ubiquitin ligase.
source: Specifically, we found that the vacuole membrane lysine transporter Ypq1 is ubiquitinated after lysine withdrawal by Rsp5, a Nedd4 family HECT-type E3 ubiquitin ligase.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work by the authors' lab.

claim: Rsp5 is recruited to the vacuole membrane by Ssh4, a PY-motif containing type-I transmembrane protein.
source: Rsp5 is recruited to the vacuole membrane by Ssh4, a PY-motif containing type-I transmembrane protein.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work by the authors' lab.

claim: After ubiquitination, Ypq1 is sorted into the vacuole lumen for degradation.
source: After ubiquitination, Ypq1 is sorted into the vacuole lumen for degradation (Li et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work by the authors' lab, supported by a citation.

claim: The zinc transporter Cot1 is ubiquitinated by Tul1, a RING-type E3 ligase, and is sorted into the vacuole lumen for degradation upon the depletion of zinc.
source: We also reported that the zinc transporter Cot1 is ubiquitinated by Tul1, a RING-type E3 ligase, and is sorted into the vacuole lumen for degradation upon the depletion of zinc (Li et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work by the authors' lab, supported by a citation.

claim: The insertion of a 38 amino acid streptavidin-binding-peptide (SBP) between Ypq1 and GFP results in constitutive sorting of Ypq1 into the vacuole lumen, even in the presence of lysine.
source: Serendipitously, we found that the insertion of a 38 amino acid streptavidin-binding-peptide (SBP) (Terpe, 2003) between Ypq1 and GFP (Ypq1-SBP-GFP) results in constitutive sorting of Ypq1 into the vacuole lumen, even in the presence of lysine (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Ypq1-SBP-GFP sorting is blocked on the vacuole membrane in a mutant lacking the vacuolar ubiquitin E3 ligase adaptor Ssh4.
source: Importantly, Ypq1-SBP-GFP sorting is blocked on the vacuole membrane in a mutant lacking the vacuolar ubiquitin E3 ligase adaptor Ssh4(Figure 1B), suggesting that Ypq1-SBP-GFP is degraded through the same vacuole membrane protein degradation pathway as Ypq1-GFP.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Ypq1-SBP-GFP is degraded through the same vacuole membrane protein degradation pathway as Ypq1-GFP.
source: Importantly, Ypq1-SBP-GFP sorting is blocked on the vacuole membrane in a mutant lacking the vacuolar ubiquitin E3 ligase adaptor Ssh4(Figure 1B), suggesting that Ypq1-SBP-GFP is degraded through the same vacuole membrane protein degradation pathway as Ypq1-GFP.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the observation that Ssh4 is required for both Ypq1-GFP and Ypq1-SBP-GFP sorting.

claim: Wild-type cells constitutively degrade Ypq1-SBP-GFP-His3 via the vacuole membrane protein degradation pathway, making them His-.
source: Cartoon depicting genetic selection: wild-type cells constitutively degrade Ypq1-SBP-GFP-His3 via the vacuole membrane protein degradation pathway. This effectively removes His3 from the cytoplasm, making WT cells His-.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 1C and supported by the growth assay in Figure 1D.

claim: Degradation mutants prevent Ypq1 sorting, leaving His3 exposed to the cytoplasm, making them His+.
source: Degradation mutants, however, prevent Ypq1 sorting, this leaves His3 exposed to the cytoplasm, making them His+.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 1C and supported by the growth assay in Figure 1D.

claim: ssh4Δ mutant cells are His+ when expressing Ypq1-SBP-GFP-His3.
source: In contrast, mutants defective for Ypq1 ubiquitination and sorting (Figure 1C, right), such as ssh4Δ, are His+ (Figure 1D) because the fused His3 persists on the cytoplasmic surface of the vacuole.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by the growth assay shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ypq1-SBP-pHluorin is quenched once sorted into the vacuole lumen because the vacuole lumen is acidic.
source: To accomplish this, we fused Ypq1-SBP to pHluorin, a pH-sensitive GFP variant that is quenched at low pH (Miesenböck et al., 1998; Prosser et al., 2010). Since the vacuole lumen is acidic, Ypq1-SBP-pHluorin is quenched once sorted into the vacuole lumen (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the screen design and supported by citations and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Ypq1 sorting mutants are fluorescent when expressing Ypq1-SBP-pHluorin.
source: This makes Ypq1 sorting mutants fluorescent, such as ssh4Δ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), whereas WT cells are quenched.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by microscopy and flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The genetic screens identified the ESCRTs, the E3 ligase RSP5 and its vacuole membrane adaptor SSH4, and the endosome-vacuole fusion machinery (HOPS/CORVET/SNAREs).
source: Using these complementary genetic approaches, as shown in the Supplemental file 2, we identified the ESCRTs, the E3 ligase RSP5 and its vacuole membrane adaptor SSH4, and the endosome-vacuole fusion machinery(HOPS/CORVET/SNAREs).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the genetic screens.

claim: The genetic screens identified the PtdIns 3-kinase complex components VPS34 and VPS15.
source: We also found the PtdIns 3-kinase complex components VPS34 and VPS15, which are essential for making PtdIns(3)P, a prerequisite for ESCRT recruitment to membranes (Katzmann et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the genetic screens, with a citation supporting the role of these components.

claim: VPS34 and VPS15 are essential for making PtdIns(3)P, a prerequisite for ESCRT recruitment to membranes.
source: We also found the PtdIns 3-kinase complex components VPS34 and VPS15, which are essential for making PtdIns(3)P, a prerequisite for ESCRT recruitment to membranes (Katzmann et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The genetic screens did not identify any vesicle coat proteins, vesicle budding machinery or ubiquitin-binding proteins (other than the ESCRT proteins).
source: Unexpectedly, despite finding the vacuole fusion machinery, we did not identify any vesicle coat proteins, vesicle budding machinery or ubiquitin-binding proteins (other than the ESCRT proteins).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the genetic screens.

claim: Ssh4-mNeonGreen is mainly localized to the vacuole membrane and lumen in WT cells.
source: As shown in Figure 2A, Ssh4-mNeonGreen is mainly localized to the vacuole membrane and lumen in WT cells.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In the ESCRT mutant vps27Δ, Ssh4 is blocked at aberrant endosomes and co-localizes with the v-ATPase component Vph1.
source: In the ESCRT mutant vps27Δ, however, Ssh4 is blocked at aberrant endosomes and co-localizes with the v-ATPase component Vph1, which is trafficked to the vacuole via the VPS pathway and accumulates at aberrant endosomes in ESCRT mutants (Gerrard et al., 2000; Piper et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2A and citations.

claim: Ssh4 requires ESCRT function to be delivered to the vacuole.
source: These data demonstrate that Ssh4 requires ESCRT function to be delivered to the vacuole, which implies that ESCRTs are required for Ypq1 ubiquitination.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that Ssh4 is mislocalized in ESCRT mutants.

claim: ESCRTs are required for Ypq1 ubiquitination.
source: These data demonstrate that Ssh4 requires ESCRT function to be delivered to the vacuole, which implies that ESCRTs are required for Ypq1 ubiquitination.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the observation that Ssh4 delivery requires ESCRTs.

claim: In WT cells after 2 hr lysine withdrawal, Ypq1 becomes polyubiquitinated.
source: In WT cells after 2 hr lysine withdrawal, there was a high-molecular-weight myc-ub signal, indicating that after lysine withdrawal Ypq1 becomes polyubiquitinated.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the ubiquitination assay shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In vps27Δ, Ypq1 polyubiquitination does not occur after lysine withdrawal.
source: In vps27Δ, however, this polyubiquitination did not occur.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the ubiquitination assay shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In ESCRT mutants, Ypq1 cannot be ubiquitinated because Ssh4 delivery to the vacuole is blocked.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that in ESCRT mutants, Ypq1 cannot be ubiquitinated because Ssh4 delivery to the vacuole is blocked (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the ubiquitination assay and Ssh4 localization data.

claim: Ypq1 is blocked at the vacuole membrane after lysine withdrawal in the endosome-vacuole fusion mutants vam3ts and vps18ts at non-permissive temperature.
source: We previously observed that Ypq1 is blocked at the vacuole membrane after lysine withdrawal in the endosome-vacuole fusion mutants vam3ts (SNARE) and vps18ts (HOPS) at non-permissive temperature (Li et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work by the authors' lab, supported by a citation.

claim: Ssh4 delivery requires endosome-vacuole fusion machinery.
source: Since Ssh4 delivery requires these fusion machineries (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), we hypothesized that the delivery of newly synthesized Ssh4 may be required and that the pre-existing vacuole membrane pool of Ssh4 may not be sufficient to ubiquitinate Ypq1 after temperature shift.
evidence: This is stated as an observation supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Endosome-vacuole fusion mutants vam3ts and vps18ts block the ubiquitination of Ypq1-GFP after lysine withdrawal.
source: As can be seen in the Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, these mutants block the ubiquitination of Ypq1-GFP after lysine withdrawal.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the ubiquitination assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Proper delivery of Ssh4 to the vacuole membrane is required for the normal ubiquitination of Ypq1-GFP.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that proper delivery of Ssh4 to the vacuole membrane is required for the normal ubiquitination of Ypq1-GFP.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations that ESCRT and fusion mutants block Ssh4 delivery and Ypq1 ubiquitination.

claim: The RapiDeg system is based on the rapamycin-induced dimerization between the human FKBP12 protein (FKBP) and the FRB domain of human mTOR (FRB).
source: The RapiDeg system is based on the rapamycin-induced dimerization between the human FKBP12 protein (FKBP) and the FRB domain of human mTOR (FRB) (Banaszynski et al., 2005; Foster and Fingar, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as the basis for the RapiDeg system and supported by citations.

claim: The addition of rapamycin induces rapid sorting of Ypq1-FKBP from the vacuole membrane into the vacuole lumen where it is degraded within 30 min.
source: As shown in Figure 2D and E, the addition of rapamycin induces rapid sorting of Ypq1-FKBP from the vacuole membrane into the vacuole lumen where it is degraded within 30 min.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy and Western blot data shown in Figures 2D and 2E.

claim: RapiDeg-induced Ypq1 degradation is much faster than degradation after lysine withdrawal, which takes 4–6 hr.
source: This is much faster than the degradation kinetics after lysine withdrawal, which takes 4–6 hr, presumably because cells consume their intracellular lysine stores before ubiquitinating Ypq1 (Li et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between RapiDeg and lysine withdrawal methods, with a citation.

claim: In the absence of FRB-3xUb, rapamycin treatment does not induce Ypq1-FKBP degradation.
source: As expected, in the absence of FRB-3xUb, rapamycin treatment does not induce Ypq1-FKBP degradation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy and Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: The RapiDeg system bypasses the requirement of Ssh4 for Ypq1 ubiquitination.
source: Importantly, the RapiDeg system bypasses the requirement of Ssh4 for Ypq1 ubiquitination (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Only Ypq1-FKBP was sorted to the vacuole lumen after rapamycin treatment in cells co-expressing Ypq1-mCherry and Ypq1-FKBP.
source: To test the specificity of the RapiDeg system, we added rapamycin to cells co-expressing Ypq1-mCherry and Ypq1-FKBP. As expected, only Ypq1-FKBP was sorted to the vacuole lumen degradation (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: After lysine withdrawal, both Ypq1-FKBP and Ypq1-mCherry were sorted into the vacuole lumen in a Ssh4-dependent manner.
source: After lysine withdrawal, both Ypq1-FKBP and Ypq1-mCherry were sorted into the vacuole lumen in a Ssh4-dependent manner (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B,C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B,C.

claim: The addition of the FKBP motif does not affect the ability of Ypq1 to respond to lysine withdrawal.
source: These results suggest that the addition of the FKBP motif does not affect the ability of Ypq1 to respond to lysine withdrawal.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that Ypq1-FKBP responds to lysine withdrawal similarly to Ypq1-mCherry.

claim: The RapiDeg system can be used to study the ubiquitin-dependent trafficking and sorting of transmembrane proteins from the PM, Golgi, and endosome, as well as other vacuole membrane proteins into the vacuole lumen for degradation.
source: Importantly, we also found that the RapiDeg system can be used to study the ubiquitin-dependent trafficking and sorting of transmembrane proteins from the PM (e.g. Can1), Golgi (e.g. Kex2), and endosome (e.g. Nhx1), as well as other vacuole membrane proteins (e.g. Vph1) into the vacuole lumen for degradation (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by microscopy and Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Vps18 is required for the tethering/fusion of biosynthetic, endocytic, and autophagic compartments with the vacuole.
source: Vps18 is required for the tethering/fusion of biosynthetic, endocytic, and autophagic compartments with the vacuole (Rieder and Emr, 1997 ; Robinson et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Vam7, Vam3, and Vti1 co-assemble at the vacuolar membrane into the t-SNARE complex, and they are required for the docking and fusion of multiple sorting intermediates destined for the vacuole.
source: Vam7, Vam3, and Vti1 co-assemble at the vacuolar membrane into the t-SNARE complex, and they are required for the docking and fusion of multiple sorting intermediates destined for the vacuole (Sato et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Ypq1-FKBP is sorted into the vacuole lumen upon cargo ubiquitination using the RapiDeg system in both vps18ts and vam7ts mutants at the non-permissive temperature.
source: We observed that Ypq1-FKBP is sorted into the vacuole lumen upon cargo ubiquitination using the RapiDeg system in both vps18ts and vam7ts mutants at the non-permissive temperature (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figures 3A and 3C.

claim: Ypq1-FKBP was degraded in the vps18ts or vam7ts mutants at non-permissive temperatures.
source: These data are consistent with the Western blot results, which demonstrated that Ypq1-FKBP was degraded in the vps18ts or vam7ts mutants at non-permissive temperatures (Figure 3B,D).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by Western blot data shown in Figures 3B and 3D.

claim: Mup1 accumulated on pre-vacuolar structures and was not degraded in vps18ts and vam7ts mutants.
source: While the vps18ts and vam7ts mutants do not block Ypq1 sorting, Mup1 accumulated on pre-vacuolar structures and was not degraded (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B and D), as expected.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy and Western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B and D.

claim: At non-permissive temperature (34°C), the sec18ts allele does not affect Ypq1 sorting into the vacuole lumen.
source: At non-permissive temperature (34°C), the sec18ts allele does not affect Ypq1 sorting into the vacuole lumen.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Ypq1 is degraded in the vacuole lumen with similar kinetics compared to WT cells in sec18ts mutant at non-permissive temperature.
source: Western blot analysis confirmed that Ypq1 is degraded in the vacuole lumen with similar kinetics compared to WT cells (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by Western blot data shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: Mup1 endocytosis was blocked in the sec18ts mutant.
source: In contrast, Mup1 endocytosis was blocked in the sec18ts mutant (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,C), confirming these conditions inactivate Sec18 function.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy and Western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: SNARE-mediated membrane fusion is not required for Ypq1 sorting into the vacuole lumen.
source: Thus, these data demonstrate that SNARE-mediated membrane fusion is not required for Ypq1 sorting into the vacuole lumen.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that Ypq1 sorting occurs in sec18ts, vps18ts, and vam7ts mutants.

claim: After shifting to non-permissive temperature and treating vps4ts cells with rapamycin, Ypq1 remained on the vacuole membrane and was not degraded.
source: After shifting to non-permissive temperature and treating vps4ts cells with rapamycin, Ypq1 remained on the vacuole membrane and was not degraded (Figure 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B), indicating that the ESCRTs are essential for the sorting of ubiquitinated Ypq1 from the vacuole membrane into the lumen.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy and Western blot data shown in Figures 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The ESCRTs are essential for the sorting of ubiquitinated Ypq1 from the vacuole membrane into the lumen.
source: After shifting to non-permissive temperature and treating vps4ts cells with rapamycin, Ypq1 remained on the vacuole membrane and was not degraded (Figure 4A,B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B), indicating that the ESCRTs are essential for the sorting of ubiquitinated Ypq1 from the vacuole membrane into the lumen.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that Ypq1 sorting is blocked in vps4ts mutants.

claim: The vacuole contains the lipid PtdIns(3)P and ubiquitinated cargo, both of which are required for ESCRT recruitment to endosomes.
source: Although the ESCRTs have not previously been shown to function on the vacuole membrane, the vacuole contains the lipid PtdIns(3)P and ubiquitinated cargo, both of which are required for ESCRT recruitment to endosomes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ESCRT recruitment requirements.

claim: GFP-FYVEVps27 localized to both vacuolar and endosomal membranes in a Vps34-dependent manner.
source: GFP-FYVEVps27 localized to both vacuolar and endosomal membranes in a Vps34-dependent manner (Figure 4C), indicating that the lipid environment of the vacuole is amenable to ESCRT recruitment.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The lipid environment of the vacuole is amenable to ESCRT recruitment.
source: GFP-FYVEVps27 localized to both vacuolar and endosomal membranes in a Vps34-dependent manner (Figure 4C), indicating that the lipid environment of the vacuole is amenable to ESCRT recruitment.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that GFP-FYVEVps27 binds to the vacuole membrane.

claim: The ESCRT machinery functions at the vacuole membrane during the sorting and degradation of Ypq1.
source: Taken together, these data support a model in which the ESCRT machinery functions at the vacuole membrane during the sorting and degradation of Ypq1.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations that ESCRTs are required for Ypq1 sorting and the vacuole has the necessary components for ESCRT recruitment.

claim: The ESCRT machinery is recruited to the vacuole membrane following Ypq1 ubiquitination.
source: This implies that the ESCRT machinery is recruited to the vacuole membrane following Ypq1 ubiquitination.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the model that ESCRTs function at the vacuole membrane.

claim: After the recruitment of FRB-3xUb to Ypq1-FKBP in ATP-depleted cells, Ypq1-FKBP sorts into many puncta at the vacuole membrane.
source: We observed that after the recruitment of FRB-3xUb to Ypq1-FKBP in ATP-depleted cells, Ypq1-FKBP sorts into many puncta at the vacuole membrane (Figure 5A top and middle).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Ypq1 does not sort into puncta in the absence of rapamycin in ATP-depleted cells.
source: Importantly, Ypq1 does not sort into puncta in the absence of rapamycin (Figure 5A bottom), indicating that the puncta are not simply due to the reduction in ATP levels.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Washing out the NaN3 and NaF restored normal Ypq1 sorting.
source: Moreover, washing out the NaN3 and NaF restored normal Ypq1 sorting (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Ypq1 degradation was blocked by ATP depletion and restored after ATP replenishment.
source: Western blot analysis further confirmed that Ypq1 degradation was blocked by ATP depletion and restored after ATP replenishment (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The inhibition of ESCRT function by NaN3/NaF treatment is not permanent and can be reversed following ATP recovery.
source: This result suggested that the inhibition of ESCRT function by NaN3/NaF treatment is not permanent and can be reversed following ATP recovery.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that Ypq1 sorting is restored after washing out NaN3/NaF.

claim: After rapamycin and NaN3/NaF treatment, Ypq1-FKBP no longer forms puncta in vps27Δ cells.
source: To test if Ypq1 puncta formation is ESCRT-dependent, we analyzed Ypq1 sorting after ATP depletion in vps27Δ cells. After rapamycin and NaN3/NaF treatment, Ypq1-FKBP no longer forms puncta.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The Ypq1-FKBP sorting intermediates are ESCRT dependent.
source: Since Vps27 is required for initiating ESCRT-mediated sorting, this suggests that the Ypq1-FKBP sorting intermediates are ESCRT dependent (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that Ypq1 puncta do not form in vps27Δ cells.

claim: After the addition of rapamycin, both Hse1-mCherry and Vps23-mCherry, were recruited to the vacuole and co-localized with the Ypq1-FKBP sorting puncta.
source: Strikingly, after the addition of rapamycin, both Hse1-mCherry and Vps23-mCherry, were recruited to the vacuole and co-localized with the Ypq1-FKBP sorting puncta (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: The ESCRT-II component Vps36-mCherry can be recruited to vacuole membrane and co-localize with Ypq1-FKBP puncta upon rapamycin treatment and ATP depletion.
source: Similarly, we observed that the ESCRT-II component Vps36-mCherry can also be recruited to vacuole membrane and co-localize with Ypq1-FKBP puncta upon rapamycin treatment and ATP depletion (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Treatment with NaN3/NaF or rapamycin alone does not lead to detectable co-localization between Ypq1-FKBP and ESCRT proteins.
source: Treatment with NaN3/NaF or rapamycin alone, does not lead to detectable co-localization between Ypq1-FKBP and ESCRT proteins (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The Ypq1-FKBP puncta do not co-localize with FM4-64-positive structures (endosomes).
source: To address whether the Ypq1-FKBP puncta that form after rapamycin treatment in ATP-depleted cells are endosomes, we stained endosomes with the lipophilic styryl dye FM4-64 (Vida and Emr, 1995). We found that the Ypq1-FKBP puncta do not co-localize with FM4-64-positive structures (endosomes) (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The ESCRT machinery can function directly on the vacuole membrane.
source: Our observations indicate that the ESCRT machinery can function directly on the vacuole membrane.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations that ESCRTs are recruited to the vacuole membrane and are required for Ypq1 sorting.

claim: The presence of both ubiquitinated cargo and PtdIns(3)P is sufficient for the recruitment of the ESCRT machinery to both the vacuole membrane and the endosome membrane.
source: Essentially, the presence of both ubiquitinated cargo and PtdIns(3)P is sufficient for the recruitment of the ESCRT machinery to both the vacuole membrane and the endosome membrane.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations that ESCRTs are recruited to the vacuole membrane when ubiquitinated cargo is present.

claim: The expression of Hse1DUB in pep12Δ cells nearly abolished the generation of ILVs.
source: The expression of Hse1DUB in pep12Δ cells, nearly abolished the generation of ILVs (Hse1DUB+/Rap-; Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by EM data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Loss of ubiquitinated cargo blocks ILV formation.
source: This is in agreement with a previous study which shows that loss of ubiquitinated cargo blocks ILV formation (MacDonald et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Rapamycin-induced ubiquitination of Ypq1-FKBP caused the accumulation of ILVs in the vacuole lumen.
source: Rapamycin-induced ubiquitination of Ypq1-FKBP caused the accumulation of ILVs in the vacuole lumen (pep12Δ, Hse1DUB+/Rap+; Figure 7C), as quantified in Figure 7E, confirming that Ypq1 is sorted from the vacuole membrane into ILVs by the ESCRT machinery.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by EM data shown in Figures 7C and 7E.

claim: Ypq1 is sorted from the vacuole membrane into ILVs by the ESCRT machinery.
source: Rapamycin-induced ubiquitination of Ypq1-FKBP caused the accumulation of ILVs in the vacuole lumen (pep12Δ, Hse1DUB+/Rap+; Figure 7C), as quantified in Figure 7E, confirming that Ypq1 is sorted from the vacuole membrane into ILVs by the ESCRT machinery.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that ILVs accumulate after rapamycin-induced Ypq1 ubiquitination.

claim: The average vesicle size of ILVs formed following rapamycin-induced Ypq1 sorting (~40 nm) were not significantly different from the ILVs formed during ILV formation at the endosome.
source: In addition, the average vesicle size of ILVs formed following rapamycin-induced Ypq1 sorting (~40 nm) were not significantly different from the ILVs formed during ILV formation at the endosome (quantified in Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by quantification shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Endosome-vacuole fusion is not required for Ypq1 sorting and degradation.
source: Here, we demonstrate that endosome-vacuole fusion is not required for Ypq1 sorting and degradation, which is inconsistent with the recycling model.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the RapiDeg experiments in fusion mutants.

claim: ESCRT complexes function directly on the vacuole surface to facilitate Ypq1 degradation.
source: Instead, we show that ESCRT complexes function directly on the vacuole surface to facilitate Ypq1 degradation, extending the role for ESCRTs in yeast.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations that ESCRTs are recruited to the vacuole membrane and are required for Ypq1 sorting.

claim: Ypq1 sorting from the vacuole membrane into the vacuole lumen after lysine withdrawal is ubiquitin dependent.
source: We have previously shown that Ypq1 sorting from the vacuole membrane into the vacuole lumen after lysine withdrawal is ubiquitin dependent.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from prior work by the authors' lab.

claim: Ypq1-SBP-GFP sorting is blocked on the vacuole membrane in ssh4Δ mutant.
source: Fluorescent microscopy analysis of cells expressing Ypq1-SBP-GFP and vacuole membrane marker Vph1-mCherry in wild-type and (B) ssh4Δ cells grown to mid-log phase at 30°C.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B where Ypq1-SBP-GFP remains on the vacuole membrane in ssh4Δ cells.

claim: Ypq1-SBP-GFP is constitutively sorted into the vacuole lumen in wild-type cells.
source: Fluorescent microscopy analysis of cells expressing Ypq1-SBP-GFP and vacuole membrane marker Vph1-mCherry in wild-type and (B) ssh4Δ cells grown to mid-log phase at 30°C.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1A where Ypq1-SBP-GFP is localized to the vacuole lumen in wild-type cells.

claim: Ubiquitinated vacuole membrane proteins are sorted directly on the vacuole membrane by the ESCRTs, which then internalize the cargo into ILVs that bud into the vacuole lumen.
source: We therefore propose that ubiquitinated vacuole membrane proteins are sorted directly on the vacuole membrane by the ESCRTs, which then internalize the cargo into ILVs that bud into the vacuole lumen.
evidence: This is stated as the proposed model based on the findings of the study.

claim: The combination of PtdIns(3)P and ubiquitinated Ypq1 on the vacuole membrane specifies the recruitment of the ESCRT-0 complex to the vacuole membrane.
source: In summary, we propose the following model (Figure 7G). The combination of PtdIns(3)P and ubiquitinated Ypq1 on the vacuole membrane specifies the recruitment of the ESCRT-0 complex to the vacuole membrane.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model shown in Figure 7G.

claim: ESCRT-0 recruitment initiates the recruitment of downstream ESCRT complexes to the vacuole membrane.
source: This event initiates the recruitment of downstream ESCRT complexes to the vacuole membrane, and ultimately results in the sorting of these cargoes into intraluminal vesicles that bud directly into the vacuole lumen.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model.

claim: ESCRT recruitment ultimately results in the sorting of cargoes into intraluminal vesicles that bud directly into the vacuole lumen.
source: This event initiates the recruitment of downstream ESCRT complexes to the vacuole membrane, and ultimately results in the sorting of these cargoes into intraluminal vesicles that bud directly into the vacuole lumen.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model.

claim: ESCRT function is ATP dependent.
source: Since ESCRT function is ATP dependent (Babst et al., 1998; Tran et al., 2009), we depleted cellular ATP levels to slow down the internalization process, and thereby help visualize sorting intermediates.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The RapiDeg system provides a tractable method for the specific inactivation (degradation) of membrane proteins in the secretory and endocytic pathways.
source: Therefore, the RapiDeg system provides a tractable method for the specific inactivation (degradation) of membrane proteins in the secretory and endocytic pathways.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the demonstrated applications of the RapiDeg system.

claim: RapiDeg should be adaptable for use in a wide range of eukaryotic organisms.
source: Importantly, RapiDeg should be adaptable for use in a wide range of eukaryotic organisms.
evidence: This is stated as speculation based on the general applicability of the rapamycin-induced dimerization system.

claim: ESCRT recruitment to the vacuole membrane uses the same components as ESCRT recruitment to the late endosome membrane, PtdIns(3)P and ubiquitinated cargo.
source: ESCRT recruitment to the vacuole membrane uses the same components as ESCRT recruitment to the late endosome membrane, PtdIns(3)P and ubiquitinated cargo.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations that both PtdIns(3)P and ubiquitinated cargo are present on the vacuole membrane and are required for ESCRT recruitment.

claim: The endosome is the major site for ILV formation due to the high concentration of ubiquitinated cargo arriving from the PM and the Golgi.
source: First, the endosome is the major site for ILV formation due to the high concentration of ubiquitinated cargo arriving from the PM and the Golgi.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for why vacuolar ESCRT pools are not easily detected under normal conditions.

claim: The large surface area of the vacuole reduces local ESCRT concentrations below detection limits.
source: Second, the large surface area of the vacuole reduces local ESCRT concentrations below our present detection limits.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for why vacuolar ESCRT pools are not easily detected under normal conditions.

claim: ESCRTs have been shown to function on various cellular membranes including HIV budding at the PM, PM wound repair, nuclear-pore assembly, nuclear envelope re-formation, and cytokinesis.
source: Recently, the ESCRTs have been shown to function on various other cellular membranes. These roles include HIV budding at the PM (Garrus et al., 2001; Martin-Serrano et al., 2001; VerPlank et al., 2001), PM wound repair (Jimenez et al., 2014), nuclear-pore assembly (Webster et al., 2014), nuclear envelope re-formation (Olmos et al., 2015; Vietri et al., 2015; Webster et al., 2014), and cytokinesis (Carlton and Martin-Serrano, 2007; Lee et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The turnover of vacuole membrane proteins revealed another subcellular location where ESCRTs function.
source: Here, the turnover of vacuole membrane proteins revealed yet another subcellular location where ESCRTs function.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the findings of the study.

claim: Doa4 is a major deubiquitinase of the endomembrane system.
source: We co-expressed Ypq1-GFP and myc-Ub in doa4Δ cells. Doa4 is a major deubiquitinase of the endomembrane system, and its deletion stabilizes ubiquitinated forms of Ypq1 (Amerik et al., 2000; Li et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Deletion of Doa4 stabilizes ubiquitinated forms of Ypq1.
source: Doa4 is a major deubiquitinase of the endomembrane system, and its deletion stabilizes ubiquitinated forms of Ypq1 (Amerik et al., 2000; Li et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The two ER membrane proteins tested (Erd2, Heh2) were not degraded using the RapiDeg system.
source: The two ER membrane proteins we tested were not degraded using the RapiDeg system (Erd2, Heh2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the limitations of the RapiDeg system.

claim: ESCRT-0 complexes preferably bind to K63-linked ubiquitin chains.
source: It was also found that ESCRT-0 complexes preferably bind to K63-linked ubiquitin chains (Nathan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: K63-linked and linear head-to-tail ubiquitins adopt equivalent open conformations.
source: It was previously reported that K63-linked and linear head-to-tail ubiquitins adopt equivalent open conformations, in which the ubiquitins do not form inter-molecular interactions like K48-linked ubiquitin chains (Komander et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Sec18 is the yeast NSF (N-ethylmaleimide Sensitive Factor) homolog and is required for disassembly of cis-SNARE complexes.
source: Sec18 is the yeast NSF (N-ethylmaleimide Sensitive Factor) homolog and is required for disassembly of cis-SNARE complexes (Jun et al., 2007; Mayer et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The vacuole membrane is inherently resistant to its luminal lipases and proteases.
source: The vacuole membrane is inherently resistant to its luminal lipases and proteases, while ILVs derived from this membrane, must be lysed in order to degrade their protein cargoes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the properties of the vacuole membrane.

claim: ILVs derived from the vacuole membrane must be lysed in order to degrade their protein cargoes.
source: The vacuole membrane is inherently resistant to its luminal lipases and proteases, while ILVs derived from this membrane, must be lysed in order to degrade their protein cargoes.
evidence: This is stated as an inference about the fate of vacuole membrane-derived ILVs.

claim: A new model for selective sorting and degradation of vacuole membrane proteins has been proposed, the intralumenal fragment (ILF) pathway.
source: Recently, a new model for selective sorting and degradation of vacuole membrane proteins has been proposed, the intralumenal fragment (ILF) pathway (McNally et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: In the ILF pathway model, vacuolar membrane proteins are sorted into the interface of two opposing vacuoles and are internalized after vacuole fusion in an ESCRT-independent manner.
source: In this model, vacuolar membrane proteins are sorted into the interface of two opposing vacuoles and are internalized after vacuole fusion in an ESCRT-independent manner.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the ILF pathway model.

claim: The ILF pathway does not play a significant role in ubiquitin-dependent sorting of Ypq1.
source: We do not think that this pathway plays a significant role in ubiquitin-dependent sorting of Ypq1, because Ypq1 sorting is ESCRT dependent, and does not require Sec18(NSF), Vps18(HOPS) and Vam7(Vacuole SNARE), which are required for vacuole-vacuole fusion (Wickner, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observations that Ypq1 sorting is ESCRT dependent and does not require vacuole fusion machinery.

claim: Sec18(NSF), Vps18(HOPS) and Vam7(Vacuole SNARE) are required for vacuole-vacuole fusion.
source: We do not think that this pathway plays a significant role in ubiquitin-dependent sorting of Ypq1, because Ypq1 sorting is ESCRT dependent, and does not require Sec18(NSF), Vps18(HOPS) and Vam7(Vacuole SNARE), which are required for vacuole-vacuole fusion (Wickner, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.
